Answer: C
Reason: Figure 1 shows diffuse bilateral alveolar opacities consistent with pulmonary edema (often seen in salt water aspiration), which completely resolve in Figure 2; this rapid clearance is characteristic of supportive care (oxygen/ventilation) allowing resorption of aspirated fluid, whereas pneumonia or cardiogenic edema typically resolves more slowly or requires specific pharmacologic intervention not implied by the complete normalization.
